html:
France Prešeren was a Slovene Romantic poet, born in 1800 in Vrba in the Upper Carniola region, who showed that Slovene could carry great poetry.

He worked as a lawyer's clerk in Ljubljana and wrote sonnets and ballads, many about his unreturned love for Julija Primic. His Baptism on the Savica is an epic of the Christianisation of the Slovenes. His collected Poems appeared in 1847. The poem Zdravljica, a toast to the friendship of nations, was cut by the censor; its seventh stanza became the anthem of Slovenia in 1989. The day of his death, 8 February, is the national culture day. He is the Slovene counterpart of Mickiewicz or Shevchenko.
